eventPool.learningNote: Cutting is controlled at source — water suppression or on-tool extraction — with face-fitted RPE as backup, never as the plan. Visible dust leaving site is both a health failure and an enforcement magnet: treat any dry-cutting discovery as a stop-and-fix, not a reminder.

eventPool.prompt: EVENT: You find that the demolition gang has removed one prop from the designed propping layout on the first floor to get the skid-steer through an opening, and stood it against the wall 'to go back after the machine's through'.

options.text: Clear and prohibit access to the affected bays above and below, stop plant movements on that slab, get the TWC and the propping designer to assess and direct reinstatement, verify it before the area reopens, and investigate why the gang could and did alter temporary works without approval.
options.feedback: Correct. The layout is a designed structure — one prop out changes the load paths for everything around it, with a machine driving over the top. Exclusion, engineered reinstatement, verification, then fix the control failure.

options.text: Have the gang stand the prop back in its position and re-tighten it, then carry on — it was only out for twenty minutes.
options.feedback: Unsafe. A prop re-stood by the gang that shouldn't have touched it, unverified against the design, may be carrying nothing — and the slab was loaded by plant while the layout was broken.
options.criticalFailure: Unauthorised propping alteration reinstated without engineering verification

options.text: Log it for the TWC's weekly temporary works walk-round on Friday and tell the gang not to do it again.
options.feedback: Four more days of plant on a slab whose propping is in an unknown state. Temporary works alterations are a now problem, not a Friday agenda item.

options.text: Remove the skid-steer from the slab as a precaution and let the gang carry on hand demolition in the area meanwhile.
options.feedback: Taking the plant load off helps, but people are still working around propping in an unverified state — the exclusion and the engineering assessment come before any work resumes there.

eventPool.topic: Temporary works — unauthorised alteration of propping
eventPool.learningNote: Nobody alters propping except under the TWC's control, to the designer's direction — and reinstatement needs verification, not good intentions. If gangs are moving props to get plant through, the design didn't allow for the plant route: fix that through the TWC, not around them.

eventPool.prompt: EVENT: A refuse lorry servicing the shops clips a leg of the pavement gantry at the kerb line. The structure looks straight from the ground, the driver wants to exchange details and go, and shoppers are walking under the gantry now.

options.text: Close and divert the footpath section under the gantry immediately, in liaison with the authority as needed; get the TWC and the gantry designer to inspect the impacted leg and connections before anyone passes back under it; record the strike, get the driver's details, and review kerb-line impact protection.
options.feedback: Correct. A struck support is unverified structure with the public beneath it — 'looks straight' is not an assessment. Close, inspect to the design, then reopen; and if a strike was possible, the impact protection needs reviewing.

options.text: Walk the gantry deck yourself — if nothing has visibly shifted up top, let the footpath stay open and report it to the scaffold contractor.
options.feedback: Impact damage hides in connections, welds and base details that a deck walk can't see. Every shopper passing underneath is trusting a structure nobody competent has verified since the strike.

options.text: Cone off just the struck leg and let pedestrians keep using the rest of the gantry width while you wait for the inspection.
options.feedback: Better than nothing, but the gantry is one structure — if the impacted leg has shed load, the deck above the walking route is relying on members now carrying loads they weren't checked for.

options.text: Take the driver's details and carry on — gantries are designed robustly and lorries brush them all the time in town.
options.feedback: Unsafe. Normalising strikes on the structure protecting the public is how a later, harder strike finds a weakened gantry. Every impact gets an engineering check — that is the deal that lets you build over a footpath.
options.criticalFailure: Public allowed under gantry after vehicle strike without engineering inspection

eventPool.learningNote: Any impact on a structure over the public means: exclude beneath, competent inspection against the design before reuse, record and report, and review the protection that let the vehicle reach it. Public protection structures get zero benefit of the doubt.

eventPool.prompt: EVENT: With skips backing up in the yard, a haulier who has 'worked this street for years' offers same-day muck-away at two-thirds of your contracted rate, cash-friendly. He can't produce a waste carrier registration — 'the office has all that'.

options.text: Decline until the paperwork exists: verify his carrier registration on the public register and the receiving site's permit, and only then consider him — meanwhile solve the backlog with your contracted carrier and better collection scheduling.
options.feedback: Correct. Duty of care means knowing who carries your waste and where it lands. Unverifiable carrier plus cash price usually equals a gateway to fly-tipping — with your transfer note, or none at all, in the load.

options.text: Use him for the inert demolition arisings only — brick and concrete can't really be fly-tipped harmfully.
options.feedback: Inert waste is fly-tipped constantly — in gateways, lay-bys and fields — and the duty of care applies to every load regardless of what it is. Your name traces back with it.

options.text: Take his details and let him do one load today on trust while the office 'sends the registration over'.
options.feedback: Once the load leaves, you've transferred waste to an unverified carrier — if it surfaces in a field gateway, the paper trail ends at your site and the offence is yours to answer.
options.criticalFailure: Waste transferred to an unverified carrier

options.text: Solve the backlog by double-stacking and compacting the yard skips until the contracted carrier's next scheduled run.
options.feedback: It keeps the waste legal but builds a fire load and overloading problem in a tiny yard next to occupied premises — the real fix is collection frequency, which is a phone call.

eventPool.topic: Waste duty of care — carrier verification
eventPool.learningNote: Before any waste leaves site: carrier registration verified (the public register takes two minutes), destination permitted, transfer or consignment note completed and kept. A price that's too good is usually priced without the landfill gate fee — which tells you where the load is really going.

modelAnswerNotes: Refurbishment and demolition asbestos survey and structural appraisal obtained before any strip or demolition planning; no intrusive work ahead of survey coverage.

Duty holders appointed in writing; F10 notified and displayed; demolition planned in writing by competent people; HSE-licensed asbestos contractor and engineered-demolition-capable contractor verified before appointment.
CPP proportionate and live, covering asbestos sequence, demolition, temporary works, fire in the stripped building and the public interface — in place before the phase started.

Site set-up: gantry and hoarding protecting the footpath; marshalled gate on the shared rear lane with booked deliveries; welfare stacked in the yard or established in the building; gas cage external; skips segregated in the yard, never in the lane; exclusion zone on the annexe; dust suppression at source.

Sequence protected people: asbestos removal with independent four-stage clearance area by area before strip; strip before machine demolition; nobody inside the exclusion zone with the machine working.

TWC appointed with stop-work authority; ten-item register with flank wall retention at cat 3 and propping, gantry and plant back-propping at cat 2 — all with hard hold points; movement monitoring with trigger levels and named escalation.
Permits: hot works, daily demolition authorisation, load/strike, asbestos clearance re-entry gate, services isolation and lifting — no dig or confined space permits padding the system.
Inspections: scaffold 7-day and after weather; gantry and hoarding after storms and strikes; monitoring read to schedule; thorough-examination certificates checked at the gate.
Fire controlled through the strip: daily waste removal, permit-controlled hot works with fire watch, temporary alarm and maintained escape routes, joint arrangements with the neighbours.

Environment: segregated waste with consignment notes for hazardous streams and verified carriers; noise consent hours agreed with the authority and policed; noise, vibration and dust monitored with trigger levels; neighbours told before disruptive works, complaints answered and closed.

Events handled by stop–exclude–get the engineer/analyst–fix the system: cracks stopped demolition, struck gantry closed the footpath, torn sheeting triggered after-weather inspection, finds triggered stop-seal-sample.

Handover: updated asbestos register (removed and retained ACMs with certificates), structural as-builts and residual risks into the H&S file; gantry and scaffold strike planned as controlled temporary works with footpath reinstatement agreed.
